fair_value_reason: Forecasters now span $317-335 (mean $327.6) on near-identical inputs: FY28 core EPS of $20.0-20.6 at 16-16.5x ($320-340), and FY28 adj FCF of $1.75-1.85B on ~100-102M diluted shares at a 5.25-5.75% yield ($312-334). Net debt is $1.64B. No input remains in factual error. I take ~$20.4 x 16.25x = ~$331 for P/E and ~$324 for FCF yield, which blends to ~$327, about 7% above spot. This is essentially the mean.

thesis_triggers.event: $211 is 12x the confirmed $17.55 FY27 core EPS guide (the pre-AI EMS multiple) and about 31% below spot. It is well under the $284-287 lows that held through the July-September 2026 AI-hardware sell-off and the post-print drop. A close there would price a guide cut like FY24's or a flat FY28 (a hyperscaler pause, consignment shift or capex digestion as UBS's +6% 2028 path arrives) together with a payables unwind. The forecasters cluster at $205-215, with a mean of $211.

supervisor_summary: The five forecasters converged in round 2: fair values of $317-335 (mean ~$327, ~7% above spot), FY28 core EPS of $20.0-20.6 at 16-16.5x, a fat left tail (~17% below $213) and a thesis break near $211 (12x the $17.55 guide). My checks confirmed the new evidence: UBS sees hyperscaler capex growth at +25% in 2027 and +6% in 2028, Jabil has a second Mississippi data-center site, and JBL's 26-year Sep-to-Sep record shows a median of +6% with a log SD of 0.41. None of it moves the distribution, so I keep the forecasters' mean ladder. The risk to watch is the late-Sept 2027 FY28 guide landing just as the market prices the 2028 capex slowdown, on a model whose growth is funded by payables.
key_drivers: FY27 guide (8-K, 2026-09-30): $44.5B revenue (+24%), 6.1% core margin, $17.55 core EPS, ~$1.6B adj FCF, ~3.7% above the $16.92 consensus. The stock is at 17.3x it vs Flex at ~25x.

AI concentration: $22.1B of AI revenue (+54%), about half the guide, with cloud/data center $17.5B (+52%). UBS sees hyperscaler capex growth at +25% in 2027 and +6% in 2028, so the late-Sept 2027 FY28 guide arrives as the market prices a slowdown.

Guide record over FY22-26: beats of about +20%, +1%, +13% and +19%, and one miss (FY24, -6% to -10%). Even after the miss year the stock fell only ~6%. Buybacks shrink shares ~3% a year, supporting FY28 core EPS of ~$20.0-20.6.

Earnings quality: FCF is flat at ~$1.6B on +24% revenue, FY26 working capital was funded by +$8B of payables (AP $14.4B vs equity $1.6B), and GAAP EPS is 26% below core. This keeps the multiple at 16-16.5x rather than at the peer level.
Base rates (26 Sep-Sep years since 2000): median +6%, 54% of years up, log SD 0.41. Both crashes of more than 50% followed multi-year run-ups and end-market busts, which is the setup to watch.
